bottom: The Democratic Governors Association is her financial base. It gave more than $1.6 million to her leadership committee in June and July, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/08/georgia-governor-race-rick-jackson-raises-13m-in-outside-money/). Her campaign then said the DGA gave $11.5 million of the $23.2 million she raised from August 1 to October 20, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/10/keisha-lance-bottoms-fundraising/). The October figures are provisional until the filing lands.

Billionaire Democrats arrived late. JB Pritzker gave $1 million to her leadership fund after the October 20 cutoff, and Michael Bloomberg gave at least $1 million, per the [AJC on October 21](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/10/pritzker-bloomberg-donate-keisha-lance-bottoms-georgia-governor/).

Her signature policy fights put her against large industries: a statewide pause on new data center construction, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/business/2026/10/poll-georgians-government-regulation-of-ai/); Medicaid expansion, per her [AJC column](https://www.ajc.com/opinion/2026/10/keisha-lance-bottoms-affordability-georgia/); and ending the 2.25 percent auto insurance premium tax, per [FOX 5](https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/keisha-lance-bottoms-georgia-governor-candidate-profile). No donors from those industries were documented on either side.

Real estate is a small but traceable bloc, at least $30,000 from commercial real estate figures through July, per [Bisnow](https://www.bisnow.com/news/atlanta/economic-development/jackson-far-outraising-bottoms-georgia-governor-race-cre-execs-donations-campaign-finance). Her record as mayor includes a long term downtown redevelopment deal.

Rick Jackson is mostly his own donor. He spent more than $108 million of his own fortune to win the nomination through June 2026, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/07/heres-how-rick-jackson-spent-108-million-in-the-republican-race-for-governor/), and his campaign accounts had raised roughly $130 million through July 31, much of it his own money, per the [AJC on October 21](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/10/pritzker-bloomberg-donate-keisha-lance-bottoms-georgia-governor/). Analysts expect about $200 million by Election Day. That is an estimate, not a filing.

His own company is the largest interest in the file. Jackson Healthcare subsidiaries have received more than $1 billion in payments from Georgia agencies since 2020 and more than $56 million in 2025 alone from Behavioral Health, Community Health and Corrections, per the [AJC on March 5, 2026](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/03/rick-jackson-promises-to-unwind-his-companys-state-contracts-if-elected/). The governor appoints the people who run those agencies.

The Republican Governors Association gave $10 million to his new leadership committee, For All Georgians Inc., about two weeks after he opened it in June 2026, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/08/georgia-governor-race-rick-jackson-raises-13m-in-outside-money/) and the [Georgia Recorder](https://cobbcountycourier.com/2026/08/gop-candidates-outraise-democrats-so-far-in-most-but-not-all-of-georgias-statewide-contests/). Months earlier he had sued to stop his primary rival from using the same kind of committee.

A live federal tax fight. The IRS says about $54 million in Jackson deductions tied to film investments were improper and assessed $16 million in penalties. Jackson is disputing both in U.S. Tax Court, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/10/keisha-lance-bottoms-and-her-husband-have-a-history-of-late-tax-payments/). He has no public position on the Georgia film tax credit in the sources read.

D.t: Keisha Lance Bottoms trails by 0.4 and wins 49% of simulations. Closing it takes about 9,110 voters switching sides, or 18,220 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +7.2 and D +6.3. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +0.2. Your best recent poll is Big Data Poll (R) at D +0.5; your worst is ActiVote at R +3.0. 8 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Fulton, a projected net 233,542 votes; DeKalb, a projected net 223,518 votes; Clayton, a projected net 81,770 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Houston, R +11.2, 1.5% of the vote; Fayette, R +3.3, 1.4% of the vote; Lowndes, R +11.6, 0.9% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Keisha Lance Bottoms runs furthest behind in Hall, Forsyth, Henry. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 68% of voters, 51 to 49, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.42 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 63% of voters, 55 to 45, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.14 points; Voters without a degree, 54% of voters, 48 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.73 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Keisha Lance Bottoms: Immigration voters 20 to 79, Small counties 28 to 70, White voters 30 to 68. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$770K cash against $4.3M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Cash: $4.3M in the bank against $770K for Keisha Lance Bottoms.
